newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Merchant in bonus issue to employees.
newsitem.headline: Merchant in bonus issue to employees.

text.p: Merchant Bank of Sri Lanka Ltd has sought stock exchange permission to issue five million bonus shares to an employee share ownership trust (ESOP), in a bid to improve profitability, a bank official said on Tuesday.
The Merchant Bank set up a ESOP scheme in 1990, which borrows funds at commercial rates from the company, to purchase and trade in MBSL shares.
"But the recent decline in the share market and in the company's shares, has resulted in the ESOP owing MBSL loans plus interest amounting to about 120 million rupees," a bank official told Reuters.
Colombo stocks took a major blow in 1995, when global funds pulled out of emerging markets. The decline continued in 1996, as company profits were hit by a drought and power cuts.
The share, which fell to a low of 10 rupees in July 1996, was trading at 21 rupees on Tuesday.
The bonus issue will enable the ESOP to profit by trading in MBSL shares, which are now recovering along with the market, the official said.
"The ESOP can then pay back the 120 million it owes MBSL, which will not have to make a provision (for bad debts) in 1997," he added.
Since the solving of EOSP problems will have a direct bearing on profitability of Merchant Bank, the share dilution by issuing bonus shares, was justified, the official said.
Unaudited results of Merchant Bank for the financial year ended 31 December 1996, show the company made a net profit of 54.93 million rupees, up from 33.79 million in 1995.
Market analysts say pulling the ESOP out of the red will boost MBSL profits by about 30 million rupees, in 1997.
The bonus issue has to be approved by a majority of 75 percent at an EGM, after getting the greenlight from the stock exchange. -- Colombo newsroom (941) 434319
